research.notes:
**Window: ~Oct 3–13, 2026. Older items are labeled. Several sources are aggregators, so I've flagged the weaker ones.**

## 1. AI-lab financing
- **Revenue miss:** OpenAI told investors annualized revenue was near $50B at end-September. That is about $20B below the ~$70B figure reported in late September. The gap came from how investors compared it with Anthropic. — https://dealroom.co/news/161093-openais-annualised-revenue-is-about-20b-below-the-70b-reported-ft-says/
- **Market reaction:** Nasdaq fell about 1.25% and Nvidia nearly 3%. — https://aiweekly.co/alerts/openai-tells-backers-revenue-nears-50b-20b-below-prior-report
- **Oracle reaction:** Oracle fell 4.9%. — https://unusualwhales.com/news/openai-50-billion-revenue
- **Conflicting report:** Bloomberg reportedly says OpenAI still expects ~$70B annualized by year-end. — https://aiweekly.co/alerts/openai-tells-backers-revenue-nears-50b-20b-below-prior-report
- **OpenAI IPO:** It has reportedly slipped to early 2027. — https://dealroom.co/news/161093-openais-annualised-revenue-is-about-20b-below-the-70b-reported-ft-says/
- **SoftBank:** It is due to complete a $10B OpenAI investment in October, largely debt-funded. — https://finance.biggo.com/news/66c0a95c-d834-4605-b4e6-de57ef1eb5fb
- **Anthropic:** No new priced round since the May $65B Series H at $965B, as of Oct 3. Its compute commitments are about $518B. — https://www.useluminix.com/reports/company-overviews/anthropic-valuation-history and https://explodingtopics.com/blog/anthropic-revenue
- **Neoclouds:** CoreWeave and Nebius fell Oct 12 on funding and valuation worries. A Nebius COO sold ~$117.8M of stock on Oct 5 under a plan adopted in May. — https://www.tipranks.com/news/coreweave-and-nebius-stocks-fall-while-iren-rises-in-premarket-today-october-12-whats-driving-the-moves
- **CoreWeave leverage:** A $4.2B convertible is described as expected, with dilution risk. Debt is about $51.6B against ~$5.5B cash. — https://rollingout.com/2026/10/13/coreweave-stock-gap-down-backlog-debt
- Nothing found this week on Mistral, xAI, Lambda or Crusoe.

## 2. Credit
- **Bank loan syndication:** JPMorgan, MUFG and others have spent over six months trying to place $38B of Oracle/Vantage construction debt. Banks are also exploring significant risk transfers. This is a low-tier aggregator citing the FT. — https://startupfortune.com/banks-are-now-trying-to-offload-the-ai-data-center-debt-they-just-underwrote/
- **Oracle and Meta bonds:** The same source says Oracle's 5-year CDS is ~203bp, an 18-year high, after S&P cut it to BBB-. It also says Meta's $25B bond drew $96B of peak orders, versus $125B for a $30B deal a year earlier. — https://startupfortune.com/bond-investors-are-starting-to-say-no-to-the-ai-debt-binge/ (unverified aggregator)
- **Spread moves, Oct 2–9:** CoreWeave widened ~70bp, mostly on Oct 8. Oracle widened ~18bp and AMD ~20bp. Meta and Broadcom each narrowed ~28bp. — https://fearprice.substack.com/p/your-ai-stock-selling-shovels-or
- **Data-center high-yield bonds:** All four issued since July sold at a discount. Oracle reportedly gave a force majeure notice on its New Mexico project. — https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/ai-data-center-financing-market-faces-credit-tightening-and-rising-costs (low-tier, undated)
- **Older context (late July):** CoreWeave's $2.6B loan repriced about 100bp wider (to SOFR+550) and was discounted to ~96. — https://marketwise.com/investing/coreweave-stock-the-2-6-billion-debt-signal-the-ai-bubble-is-ignoring/

## 3. Suppliers
- **Micron (Sept 30):** Revenue was $54.23B against $51.07B expected. The Q1 guide is ~$61.5B against $57B expected. — https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/30/micron-mu-q4-earnings-report-2026.html
- **Micron wording:** Prepared remarks cite "modestly lower rate of content growth than prior expectations" for servers, amid tight supply. — https://s25.q4cdn.com/621799436/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/Q4-FY26-Prepared-Remarks.pdf
- **TSMC:** Apple, Nvidia and others reportedly raised 2nm orders 10–20%. — https://invezz.com/news/2026/09/28/tsmc-stock-slips-despite-2nm-boom-why-apple-and-nvidia-are-raising-orders/
- **Broadcom:** FY27 estimates saw 25 downward and 11 upward revisions over 30 days. Nvidia's saw 42 up and none down. — https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/07/nvidia-or-broadcom-in-october-1-ai-chip-stock-gets-my-money/
- **Credo:** Down 17% over the past month despite an earnings beat. — https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/01/ai-spending-is-entering-its-next-phase-this-stock-could-benefit-most/
- **Insider selling:** Nvidia director Mark Stevens sold ~$947M in Q3, and Arista CEO Jayshree Ullal was also a top-10 seller. — https://qz.com/nvidia-mark-stevens-ai-insider-stock-selling-third-quarter-100726
- **Insider buying:** Nvidia insiders bought only $250K over five years. — https://www.thestreet.com/investing/nvidia-palantir-alphabet-insider-stock-sales
- No "pacing/digestion" language found. Nothing found this week on AMD, SK Hynix, Vertiv, Arista, Astera or Celestica.

## 4. Physical build-out
- **Texas:** ERCOT has halted energizing new large-load (≥75MW) data-center interconnections pending an audit. — https://energyinfrastructurepulse.sidley.com/2026/09/23/governor-abbotts-environmental-permitting-freeze-expands-pause-on-texas-data-center-development-to-all-texas-data-centers-pending-statewide-audit/
- **Texas permits:** On Sept 21 the governor told TCEQ to suspend data-center permits. TCEQ's compliance report is due Oct 19. — https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/puct-sets-financial-commitments-data-center-interconnection-governor-pauses-permit
- **FERC (Oct 9):** It rejected most of PJM's large-load interconnection plan. — https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-large-load-interconnection-iras-byonc/832716/
- **Cancellations:** A tracker lists 59 cancelled projects. These include a 1,000MW Henderson, NV project withdrawn in Sept and AWS's 500MW Calvert Cliffs withdrawn in Aug. — https://programs.com/resources/data-center-project-tracker/
- **GPU rental prices:** Roughly stable. The median H100 on-demand price is flat over 90 days and ~13% above a year ago. — https://getdeploying.com/gpus/nvidia-h100
- **Ohio politics:** Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy vowed to halt approvals of new data-center projects. — https://www.cbsnews.com/news/data-center-boom-republicans-2026-midterm-elections/
- Nothing found on turbine or transformer order changes this week.

## Positives
- **Capex guidance:** Every tracked hyperscaler raised or held guidance in the Q2 round. Alphabet is at $195–205B and Amazon at ~$220B. — https://supercyclehq.com/blog/reports/hyperscaler-capex-september-2026
- **Nvidia–OpenAI:** A July WSJ report said Nvidia was in talks on a ~$250B lease and debt guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio project. — https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/coreweave-and-nebius-shares-rise-on-nvidiaopenai-financing-talks-93CH-4813567
- **Nebius:** It targets 5GW contracted by year-end. — https://supercyclehq.com/blog/reports/hyperscaler-capex-september-2026

**Net read:** Demand and supplier signals remain strong. The warning signs this week were credit appetite, the OpenAI revenue reset, and Texas and PJM grid and permit friction.

assessment.headline: OpenAI revenue reset and AI-specific credit strain emerge while supplier demand and hyperscaler capex stay strong.
assessment.digest_markdown:
**Baseline week.** This is the first assessment, so there is no prior week to compare against.

**What happened**

- **The money side wobbled.** OpenAI reportedly told investors its annualized revenue was near $50B, about $20B below an earlier reported figure. Nasdaq, Nvidia and Oracle fell on the news. A conflicting report says OpenAI still expects about $70B by year-end, and its IPO has reportedly slipped to 2027.
- **Neoclouds came under pressure.** CoreWeave and Nebius sold off on funding worries, with CoreWeave carrying roughly $51.6B of debt.
- **Credit is the clearest warning.** High-yield spreads widened 0.40 points in four weeks. Reports also say banks are struggling to offload Oracle-linked data-center loans and Oracle's default-insurance cost is at multi-year highs. Some of these sources are weak.
- **Real demand still looks strong.** Micron beat expectations and raised guidance, and TSMC orders were reportedly raised. Taiwan AI-server suppliers grew a median 77% year over year in September. Hyperscaler capex rose 22% quarter over quarter, and every tracked hyperscaler held or raised guidance.

**Why it matters**

Spending itself is not slowing. The risk is that the companies funding it are leaning harder on borrowing. Alphabet, Amazon and Oracle all had negative free cash flow last quarter. If lenders get pickier, capex plans could be trimmed later.

The macro backdrop adds pressure: the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.22% and Brent crude is about $125.

**Grid friction**

Texas has paused new large data-center hookups, and FERC rejected PJM's large-load plan. These slow construction but do not signal falling demand.

**Bottom line:** early-stage financing stress, not a pullback. Not investment advice.
